name: HELYON
subtitle: Guitar rig editor & remote
promotionalText: See your signal chain, adjust your tone and switch snapshots from your phone or tablet. A free, independent editor for compatible Helix Stadium hardware.
description:
Edit your rig from your phone or tablet.

HELYON is a free, independent editor and remote for Helix Stadium and Helix Stadium XL. Connect over local Wi-Fi or compatible USB networking to arrange effects, adjust parameters and save presets to your device.

SEE YOUR SIGNAL CHAIN
Follow your routing across both paths. Add, replace, bypass and reorder blocks, with a clear view of parallel paths.

GET THE DETAILS RIGHT
Adjust amp and effect parameters with touch controls and precise value entry. On iPad, keep the signal chain in view while working in the docked editor.

SWITCH SOUNDS
Browse presets and setlists, recall snapshots and use performance controls designed for quick access.

ACCESSIBLE CONTROLS
Choose a list layout and step controls, with support for VoiceOver and TalkBack.

TRY IT FIRST
The offline preview lets you explore block editing without connecting hardware. It does not produce audio.

REQUIREMENTS
Live editing requires Helix Stadium or Helix Stadium XL with Remote Access enabled. Connect over the same Wi-Fi network, or use compatible USB networking with Stadium firmware 1.4 or later and a data cable. Original Helix and HX devices are not supported.

Back up your presets before editing. An optional extended DSP budget is off by default, requires confirmation and resets when you disconnect. It does not add processing power and may cause rejected edits, audio dropouts or instability. Use a spare preset.

No account, advertising or analytics. Preset editing happens directly between HELYON and your device.

HELYON is not affiliated with or endorsed by Line 6 or Yamaha. Helix, Helix Stadium, Line 6 and Yamaha are trademarks of their respective owners. Product names identify compatible hardware.
reviewNotes:
HELYON is an independently developed editor and remote for user-owned Helix Stadium and Stadium XL hardware. Its App Store name is now HELYON. References to compatible hardware identify which devices the app supports; the app does not claim affiliation with or endorsement by Line 6 or Yamaha.

I am Dwayne Charrington, the author of the MIT-licensed helix-stadium-tools project:
https://github.com/Vheissu/helix-stadium-tools
HELYON uses my implementation of local device control. It connects directly over the user's local network or compatible USB networking after the owner enables Remote Access. There is no Line 6 login or cloud-service integration. The app does not install firmware.

For relevant context, the App Store currently lists Stadium Remote:
https://apps.apple.com/us/app/stadium-remote/id6822839254
It advertises local control and preset editing for the same hardware. Its developer, Camryn, contacted me for permission to release an app using my open-source code. I am providing this comparison to clarify the interoperability use case, not as a claim about another developer's authorization arrangements.

This submission includes a redesigned interface and new screenshots captured from the app. The earlier replacements of the 24 category/connection icons and copied parameter-help text remain in place. Song upload and its associated transfer module and credentials remain removed.

Please assess this submission as an independent controller for the user's own hardware. If guideline 5.2.1 still applies, please identify the specific content, naming or control functionality requiring a change, and the documentation required. I would welcome a review discussion if that would help resolve the remaining concern.

Review without hardware: tap Try offline preview on the connection screen. The preview supports local block and parameter editing but does not produce audio or simulate hardware saving, song playback, setlists or DSP behaviour.

Live editing: enable Remote Access on the Stadium, connect to the same Wi-Fi network, and allow Local Network access. Select the device or enter its name/IP address. Compatible USB networking requires Stadium firmware 1.4+ and a data cable. Use a spare preset and wait for Saved to Stadium before switching presets.

DSP figures are catalogue estimates, not live CPU readings. Extended DSP budget is an optional advanced setting, off by default with a warning and reset on disconnect. It raises the app estimate from 66 to 82 per path; it does not modify firmware or remove device validation.
